heard: a $125 million orbiter vanished because engineers forgot to convert units. After a nine-month journey, the Mars Climate Orbiter prepared for orbital insertion in September 1999. Communication with the probe was permanently lost as navigators searched for answers. An investigation revealed builder Lockheed Martin supplied impulse data in pound-force seconds. Meanwhile, NASA's navigation software in California expected all incoming metrics in Newton seconds. One pound force is equal to 4.45 Newtons, multiplying small thruster forces into a fatal error. This mismatch plunged the spacecraft down to an altitude of only 57 kilometers. Surpassing 80 kilometers was the minimum survival altitude before the orbiter was destroyed. Engineers forgot simple unit conversions, meaning a $125 million dollar orbiter vanished.
